title: Happy Number

concept.title: Detect a cycle with a set
body: Replace a number by the sum of the squares of its digits, and repeat. Either you reach 1 (and stay there, the number is *happy*), or the numbers **fall into a loop** that never contains 1. You cannot know how long to wait, but you can notice a loop: when a number appears a second time, the sequence has started to repeat.

body.code:
seen = set()
while n != 1 and n not in seen:
    seen.add(n)
    n = sum(int(d) ** 2 for d in str(n))
happy = (n == 1)

body: The set of visited values is the general tool for detecting loops in any process that is repeated, as long as the number of possible states is limited. Here the numbers fall below 1000 quickly, so the loop is always found fast.

statement: Start with a positive integer. Replace it by the sum of the squares of its digits, and repeat the step. If the process reaches 1, the number is **happy**; if it ends up in a cycle that does not contain 1, it is not. Print `yes` if the starting number is happy and `no` otherwise.
hints: Write a step that adds the squares of the digits.
Remember every value you have visited in a set.
Stop when the value is 1 (happy) or when it is already in the set (a loop).

explanation: Every visited value is stored in a set. Reaching a stored value again means the sequence loops without ever reaching 1.
solution.complexity: Time O(log n) steps in practice, space O(1) (the sequence is short).

code.python:
n = int(input())

seen = set()
while n != 1 and n not in seen:
    seen.add(n)
    total = 0
    while n > 0:
        total += (n % 10) ** 2
        n //= 10
    n = total
print("yes" if n == 1 else "no")
